title: Opportunity-cost headcount redeployment & pricing sensitivity (Jan 2027)
summary: Working sheet to estimate the opportunity cost of redeploying HC from feature teams into capacity/cost operations versus preserving product headcount and using price increases / commitment tiers to hit margin targets. Combines a simplified P&L delta per 100 FTE shifts, token-level unit economics, and a set of pricing-floor triggers that tie to committed capacity. Not final — this is a lightweight simulator for leadership discussion and negotiation with sales/ops.
key_objectives: 1) Quantify net margin impact of moving X engineers from product to capacity ops vs. raising hosted API price by Y%. 2) Provide a stepwise decision ladder for when to (a) redeploy HC, (b) raise price, or (c) accept margin compression and buy GPU spot/reserve. 3) Surface short-term cash runway implications and long-term product delivery risk.
assumptions: Base assumptions used across scenarios: (a) average hosted API blended yield = $0.0018 per token (rev), (b) weighted average token cost on current infra stack = $0.0009 per token, (c) one senior infra engineer fully redeployed reduces per-token cost by 0.00003 on peak workloads via batching/kernel tuning (gradual), (d) engineering ramp/impact lag = 6-12 weeks, (e) hiring substitution cost for contractor = 1.3x salary, (f) enterprise contracts respond to price shifts with elasticity -0.4 in base segment and -0.8 in small-mid customers. These are intentionally conservative for planning.

headcount_plan_text:
Short table (not HR-authoritative) summarizing redeploy options and downstream risk: 
- Option A (Light redeploy): Move 2 infra engineers + 1 SRE from feature teams for 6 months. Pros: immediate ops uplift; Cons: 3 product sprints delayed (est). Estimated cost savings: ~$320k TTM; product velocity impact: ~10% backlog delay.
- Option B (Moderate redeploy): Move 5 engineers (infra/SRE/DevTools) for 9 months + hire 2 contractors for product. Savings: ~$820k TTM; velocity impact: ~20% backlog friction.
- Option C (Deep redeploy): Move 10 engineers for 12 months, freeze one product hire cycle. Savings: ~$1.9M TTM; velocity impact: major roadmap deferral risk (feature SLAs at risk).
Each option includes a reallocation playbook: ramp, measurement of per-token delta, rollback triggers tied to latency/mistmatch alerts in console.
pricing_sensitivity_notes: We model three pricing levers: percent on-hosted API, commitment-tier floors (discount vs commit), and enterprise uplift (SLA/priority features). Key observations: (1) Small-mid customers are price sensitive; >6% across-the-board increase causes outsized churn in self-serve channel. (2) A targeted enterprise uplift (add-on SLA + 12% price) nets higher margin with limited churn if paired with rollouts and grandfathering. (3) Commitment tiers reduce churn leakage and allow more predictable capacity planning; effectiveness depends on enforcement (overage pricing) and sales incentives.
unit_economics_snippet:
Back-of-envelope per-token impact assumptions: 
- Revenue per token (avg blended): $0.0018
- Token infra cost baseline: $0.0009
- Redeploy scenario per-token improvement (per senior eng): 0.00003–0.00006 (gradual)
- Net margin per token baseline: 0.0009 (50%)
Example: Aggressive-ops (8 FTE => 0.00020 TAC reduction) increases margin from 0.0009 to 0.00110 per token (~22% margin uplift), assuming no price change.
sensitivity_results_brief: When we sweep redeploy FTE from 0 to 12 and price delta from -2% to +12% across reasonable combos, two dominant regimes emerge: (A) infra-first (redeploy-heavy) maintains product velocity but risks roadmap; best for mid-term runway conservation when enterprise growth is flat. (B) price-first preserves product org but risks self-serve growth; best when sales can protect ARR in enterprise segments and when elasticity behavior holds. Hybrid combos often dominate single-lever moves in TTM margin and runway metrics.
recommendation: Short term: run Moderate redeploy (Option B) paired with a targeted enterprise price + commitment tier pilot for new enterprise deals. This gives a balanced margin uplift while preserving product roadmap with contractors. Medium term (next 6-12 months): invest in automation/ops tooling that converts redeploy gains into lasting cost-of-served improvements so redeploy is not permanent headcount drag. Put a 6-week review gate with SRE/product leads to validate velocity impact and rollback if backlog slip >15%.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: underestimated customer elasticity => larger churn. Mitigation: staged enterprise-only price pilot with clear grandfather windows.
Risk: redeploy causes feature regression. Mitigation: ring-fence critical feature owners and use contractors to backfill.
Risk: savings not realized on infra due to hardware price increase. Mitigation: conservative 60% realization buffer and regular kernel/tuning milestones.
next_steps: 1) Share with CFO + GTM lead for pricing pilot approval (target week of 2026-12-06). 2) Instrument two dashboards in Redwood Console: per-route token cost and per-team feature-velocity delta. 3) Build a short A/B on commitment tier language for enterprise quoting. 4) Re-run model with actual Q4 usage shapes (due: 2026-12-15).
